title: Moi language
text: The Moi language comprises two closely related but distinct varieties, Moi Kelim (ISO 639-3: mxn) and Moi Lemas (ISO 639-3: sbg), both West Papuan languages belonging to the West Bird's Head family, spoken primarily by the Moi ethnic group in the Sorong Regency of Southwest Papua, Indonesia, on the western part of the Bird's Head Peninsula and eastern Salawati Island.[3] Moi Kelim has an estimated 4,600 speakers based on 1993 data, while Moi Lemas has about 1,200 speakers from 1988 data; the Moi people number around 5,000 in total per older estimates, though broader census figures suggest up to 21,000 for the ethnic group as of 2010.[1][4] Initial linguistic documentation of Moi occurred in the mid-20th century amid broader surveys of Papuan languages in former Dutch New Guinea.
